lines: The [[Definition:Quaternion|set of quaternions]] $\Bbb H$ forms an [[Definition:Algebra over Field|algebra]] over the [[Definition:Field of Real Numbers|field of real numbers]].
:$(1): \quad$ An [[Definition:Associative Algebra|associative algebra]], but '''not''' a [[Definition:Commutative Algebra (Abstract Algebra)|commutative algebra]].

The [[Definition:Quaternion|quaternions]] $\Bbb H$ are formed by the [[Definition:Quaternion/Construction from Cayley-Dickson Construction|Cayley-Dickson Construction]] from the [[Definition:Complex Number|complex numbers]] $\C$.
From [[Complex Numbers form Algebra]], we have that $\C$ forms:
From [[Cayley-Dickson Construction forms Star-Algebra]], $\Bbb H$ is a [[Definition:Star-Algebra|$*$-algebra]].
From [[Cayley-Dickson Construction from Nicely Normed Algebra is Nicely Normed]], $\Bbb H$ is a [[Definition:Nicely Normed Star-Algebra|nicely normed $*$-algebra]].
From [[Cayley-Dickson Construction from Commutative Associative Algebra is Associative]], $\Bbb H$ is an [[Definition:Associative Algebra|associative algebra]].
Now suppose $\Bbb H$ formed a [[Definition:Commutative Algebra (Abstract Algebra)|commutative algebra]].
Then from [[Cayley-Dickson Construction from Real Star-Algebra is Commutative]], that would mean $\C$ is a [[Definition:Real Star-Algebra|real $*$-algebra]].
But from [[Complex Numbers form Algebra]] it is explicitly demonstrated that $\C$ is '''not''' a [[Definition:Real Star-Algebra|real $*$-algebra]].
So $\Bbb H$ can not be a [[Definition:Commutative Algebra (Abstract Algebra)|commutative algebra]].
As $\times$ is [[Definition:Commutative Operation|commutative]] on $\C$, it follows that $\tuple {1, 0} \times \tuple {x_1, x_2} = \tuple {x_1, x_2}$.
So $\tuple {1, 0} \in \C^2$ functions as a [[Definition:Unit of Algebra|unit]].
That is, $\tuple {\C^2, \times}$ is a [[Definition:Unitary Algebra|unitary algebra]].
From [[Inverses for Complex Multiplication]], every element of $\struct {\C, \times}$ except $0$ has a [[Definition:Multiplicative Inverse|multiplicative inverse]].
So $\struct {\C, \times}$ is a [[Definition:Division Algebra|division algebra]] and hence a [[Definition:Unitary Division Algebra|unitary division algebra]].

This is a [[Definition:Norm on Vector Space|norm]] because:

:$
orm {x 	imes y} = \size {x 	imes y} = \size x 	imes \size y = 
orm x 	imes 
orm y$
and so $\struct {\C^2, \times}$ is a [[Definition:Normed Division Algebra|normed division algebra]].
